text:
alex: heads-up — customer hit a crash when using the JS SDK inside a Next middleware on Vercel Edge: "ReferenceError: require is not defined"

sam: yeah edge runtime doesn't have require/ CommonJS. Are we still defaulting to CJS in package.json? :thinking_face:

alex: our published package currently has "main" -> ./dist/index.cjs and "module" missing for the ESM build. repro is literally `const client = require('@redwood/inference')` in middleware and it bombs.

ben: quick workaround on their side is dynamic import: `const { Redwood } = await import('@redwood/inference')` but that trips a lot of TS users because of default vs named export mismatches.

lina: +1 — we should ship an explicit ESM entrypoint that is tiny and doesn't pull node-only shims. propose: add `exports` map in package.json with `{"import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs","require":"./dist/cjs/index.cjs","./edge":"./dist/edge/entry.mjs"}` so bundlers and edge runtime pick the right file.

ryan: also watch for polyfills — Next Edge has global fetch but not node's AbortController shape we depend on. we pulled in `node-abort-controller` in the esm build which forces extra code in edge bundles. need an edge build that assumes globals.

alex: example fix for docs (short snippet):
```js
// middleware.ts (edge)
export default async function middleware(req) {
  const { Redwood } = await import('@redwood/inference/edge');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  const res = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(res));
}
```

sam: good. Also typing SNAFU: TS consumers get "Cannot find module" or wrong types when we only ship types for CJS. We need to expose `types`/`exports.types` per subpath so editors resolve correctly.

ben: small checklist I scribbled: 1) build and publish an ESM-only dist that avoids node shims 2) add `exports` map with explicit subpath `./edge` 3) produce `.d.ts` for each entry 4) add tests that bundle with esbuild target for edge and run in Vercel-ish runner 5) update README with edge import examples.

lina: can we detect runtime automatically (edge vs node) and export a thin factory? tempting but brittle — better to be explicit and document `@redwood/inference/edge`.

alex: agree. auto-detect caused issues before (process undefined vs shimmed). explicit path is simpler for support.

ryan: for CI, add a workflow that runs `esbuild --bundle src/entry.ts --platform=browser --target=es2020` and tries importing the bundle in a tiny jsdom-less runner. catches bundling-time node-polyfill leaks.

deploy-bot: deploy preview for docs updated — PR #924 (edge entry docs) deployed to branch `docs/edge-entry` :white_check_mark:

sam: action items: alex create issue with the package.json diff + example build, ben add TS types mapping, ryan add esbuild CI job, lina update docs + add snippet. i'll assign. :rocket:

alex: created issue #1287 and pushed a draft PR with exports map. attaching small test case in the PR. will ping once green. thanks all! :thumbsup:
